html:
A Catholic catechism printed in Manila in 1593 in Spanish and Tagalog, one of the first books printed in the Philippines. A second Doctrina Christiana in Chinese came out the same year.

The Spanish Tagalog book is credited to the Franciscan friar Juan de Plasencia. It gives the basic prayers and teachings of the Catholic Church in Spanish, then in Tagalog written in Latin letters, and again in baybayin, the old Philippine script. It was printed from carved wooden blocks, the way Chinese books were made, probably by Chinese craftsmen of Manila. The Chinese version was prepared by the Dominicans Juan Cobo and Miguel de Benavides for the Chinese merchants of the city.

The only known copy of the Tagalog book is in the Library of Congress in Washington. It is a key source for baybayin and early Tagalog. Printing reached Manila half a century after the printing press in Mexico, since the Philippines were ruled through New Spain.
sum: A Catholic catechism printed in Manila in 1593 in Spanish and Tagalog, one of the first books printed in the Philippines. A second Doctrina Christiana in Chinese came out the same year.
